questions.question_text: How many spheres of $10$ cm diameter can be completely painted with $1$ L of paint if the paint covers $1\text{ m}^{2}$?

options.why: Used the diameter $10$ as the radius, giving an area of $400\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$ per sphere and only $7$ complete spheres.
Rounded the count $31.8309\ldots$ up, although there is not enough paint to completely paint the next sphere.

questions.solution_text:
$r = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ cm}$
Area of one sphere: $4\pi(5)^{2} = 100\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
Paint coverage: $1 \times 100^{2} = 10000\text{ cm}^{2}$
$10000 \div (100\pi) = 31.8309\ldots$
The paint can completely paint $31$ spheres.
